title: Why I won’t leave mathematics, despite AI solving centuries-old problems | Ken Ono
summary: I believe human judgment remains essential Last year, I nearly quit mathematics. On 20 November, Levent Alpöge announced that, working with Claude, he had proved the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old problem about the distribution of prime numbers. The Lean and Mathlib communities have since certified the formal proof. We are only beginning to understand the argument. What kind of future awaits someone beginning a life in mathematics? In May 2025, I led the number theory team for Epoch AI’s FrontierMath project. We wrote difficult problems to test large language models. I watched an unreleased ChatGPT model compute all the moments of Tamagawa numbers of elliptic curves, drawing on work by Manjul Bhargava and Roger Heath-Brown, and on papers my father wrote in the 1960s. I was stunned. Ken Ono is a number theorist and professor of mathematics at the University of Virginia, currently on leave as founding mathematician at Axiom Math. A former vice-president of the American Mathematical Society, he is known for his work on Ramanujan and integer partitions. title: How to design an agent harness
summary: I sit down with Jon Noronha, co-founder and chief product officer of Gamma, to break down agent harnesses and the startup openings around them. Jon explains how Gamma rebuilt its product as a creative agent this year and walks me through the roughly 20 models and 200 calls behind one finished presentation. We talk about AI smell, why taste carries more weight than evals in creative work, how Gamma tests a new model within the hour, and the fast mode test that lost to good friction. Jon also shares the harnesses he wants to see, from a Slack agent that learns his voice to a couch shopping tool that checks the fit in your room. If you want to build a vertical agent, this episode gives you a clear model of what a harness is and where your edge can come from. This episode was made possible thanks to Anthropic (the team behind Claude) for hosting us at Claude Founder house and sponsoring the episode. Numbered Section Summaries 1. What is an Agent Harness Gamma started in 2020, took off in 2023, and spent this year rebuilding its product from preset LLM workflows into an agent. Jon defines the harness as the tools an agent uses to act in its environment, inspect its own work, and ask the user for preferences, with Claude Code as the best-known example for programming. I call harnesses the new wrappers, and Jon agrees, since the wrapping is most of the work and even OpenAI and Anthropic put heavy effort into harness development. 2. Inside One Gamma Prompt When someone pastes messy notes and asks for 20 slides, Gamma spins up a cloud sandbox, asks a few questions through a form, and pulls context from Notion, Slack, or Linear. It writes an outline, picks a template with vision models and embedding search, then generates text, layouts, images, and charts in parallel in about a minute.
